subject: Operational assertion: VPC isolation & token-retention controls
messages:
From: Sylvia Kwan <sylvia.kwan@medsys.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@procurecorp.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Oct 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Request: confirmation of VPC isolation + token retention schedules

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As part of our security review we need an operational assertion that: 1) customer workloads for MedSys will be deployed in an EU-only VPC/region; 2) there are tenant-isolation controls at the network and hypervisor layer (we got some answers in the SIG but need concrete evidence); and 3) short-lived token handling and retention policies are documented (we need the retention matrix for ephemeral API tokens and any audit logging retention).

Can you confirm these items and attach a snapshot of the VPC configuration and a token-retention matrix we can include in our security packet? Also flag any SLA exceptions or known gaps for EU-only traffic (e.g., control plane callbacks from non-EU regions).

Appreciate it — target for our compliance gate: next Tuesday.

Best,
Sylvia
Security & Compliance Lead
MedSys

Attachment: none (request)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Kwan <sylvia.kwan@medsys.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Oct 2025 10:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: confirmation of VPC isolation + token retention schedules

Hi Sylvia — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: EU-only hosting is supported for MedSys under the proposed Dedicated capacity plan; we have tenant isolation at the VPC and hypervisor boundaries and we can produce a signed configuration snapshot. For ephemeral tokens, we issue short-lived bearer tokens by default (default TTL = 1 hour) and keep audit logs for 90 days by standard tier; we can provide a retention matrix and call out any exceptions.

Irene/Karthik — can you assemble the evidence packet (1) VPC configuration snapshot for the EU deployment with subnet/CIDR and peering info, (2) a short statement of tenant isolation controls (network + compute), (3) token retention matrix and sample audit log entry. Please include any integration callbacks that cross regions (control plane) and whether those contain customer data.

Sylvia — aiming to send the packet by EOD Monday; if anything needs a higher-priv sign-off we9ll flag it.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
VP Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none (internal ask)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Oct 2025 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: confirmation of VPC isolation + token retention schedules

Markus/Karthik — assembling the packet now. Quick notes on scope and evidence items:

- VPC snapshot: pulled from infra-config at 2025-10-12T22:00Z; includes region eu-west-1, VPC IDs, subnets, route tables, peering connections to MedSys dedicated peer (if enabled), and security group references. Will attach PDF snapshot and a short explanation of how we enforce subnet tenancy.
- Tenant isolation: we9ll produce a 1-page bullet list: (a) per-tenant VPC peering + no shared subnets by default on Dedicated; (b) compute isolation via namespace+cgroup separation on dedicated nodes; (c) disk encryption per-tenant with customer-managed KMS option — note: KMS partitioning by key scope documented.
- Token retention: default ephemeral token TTLs = 1 hour, refresh tokens not used in server-server flows (we use signed JWTs for service identities). Audit logs (control plane + access tokens) retained 90 days on standard; we can offer 365 days as paid add-on. I will include the retention matrix spreadsheet and a sample log line (redacted).

Questions for Markus: do we want to proactively call out the control-plane callbacks that reach our US-based telemetry collector (they do not contain PII but include operation-level telemetry) or keep that in the appendix? MedSys asked explicit EU-only hosting; transparency would be better.

Irene
Sr. Security PM, Redwood Inference

Attachment: preparing 2 files
From: Sylvia Kwan <sylvia.kwan@medsys.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Oct 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: confirmation of VPC isolation + token retention schedules

Thanks Irene — transparency is appreciated. Please include the control-plane callback detail in the appendix and explicitly state whether the callback payloads include any customer data or only operational telemetry. For our internal auditors, a short yes/no plus a sample redacted log line is ideal.

Also, for the token retention policy: confirm whether API bearer tokens (used by our integration tests) ever appear in persistent logs or are explicitly redacted. If there9s a place they could persist due to debugging traces, call it out.

Sylvia

(Also looping Tom from procurement — want to make sure there are no EU-data residency clauses that conflict with contract language.)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Kwan <sylvia.kwan@medsys.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Oct 2025 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: confirmation of VPC isolation & token-retention controls (evidence packet)

Sylvia — attaching the evidence packet per Markus/Irene

Attachments:
- redwood_vpc_config_snapshot-20251012.pdf (PDF) 
- token_retention_matrix-20251012.xlsx (XLSX)
- sample-audit-log-redacted.txt (TXT)

Summary (top lines):
- Deployment region: eu-west-1 only for the Dedicated cluster provisioned for MedSys (no compute cores provisioned outside the region).
- Network isolation: dedicated VPC + dedicated subnets; peering is single-direction to customer-managed transit (customer controls peering acceptance). Security groups are tenant-scoped.
- Control-plane callbacks: our telemetry pings are routed to a telemetry collector that is EU-hosted for this Dedicated offering; an engineering exception exists for historical alerting URLs that will be removed by Nov-2025; callbacks do not include customer PII. Appendix includes sample redacted JSON of telemetry payload.
- Token handling: ephemeral bearer tokens are short-lived (TTL 1 hour) and are redacted from persisted traces by default; any debugging trace that could contain tokens is sanitized and flagged for deletion; audit logs include token event metadata but not raw token strings. Retention: control-plane logs 90 days (standard), 365 days available as contract add-on.

If you need a signed attestation, we can produce a short sign-off (Irene + infra lead) for your compliance packet.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
